tests.title: A config without the new keys loads with workers 2 and retain 720h, and in-range values load as given
given: a config.toml with only the core's keys
tests.when: the config is loaded; then loaded again with [workers].count = 64 and [database].retain = "1h" and with count = 1 and retain = "8760h"
then: defaults are count 2 and retain 720h
the boundary values 1, 64, 1h and 8760h are accepted
tests.pseudocode: c = Load(minimal); assert c.Workers.Count == 2 and c.Database.Retain == 720h; for b in bounds: assert Load(b) ok

tests.title: An out-of-range or malformed workers/retain value stops the binary with exit 2, an ERROR naming the key and no listener
given: the built agent-fox binary and a temp config directory
tests.when: the binary is started with count = 0, 65, "two" and with retain = "30m", "8761h", "soon"
then: each run exits with code 2
stderr holds an ERROR record that names workers.count or database.retain respectively
the configured listen address never accepts a connection
tests.pseudocode: for cfg in bad: r = run(binary, cfg); assert r.exit == 2; assert 'ERROR' in r.log and key in r.log; assert not dial(listen)

tests.title: Starting the service creates the three af_ tables beside jobqueue's tables and an attempts directory with mode 0700
given: a fresh temp dir with no database file
tests.when: the store opens, migrations run and the jobs service starts
then: af_jobs, af_attempts and af_events exist
jobqueue's own tables exist in the same file
attempts/ beside the database file has mode 0700
a second start with the directory present leaves it unchanged
tests.pseudocode: svc = Start(dir); assert tables ⊇ {af_jobs,af_attempts,af_events}; assert stat(dir/attempts).Mode().Perm()==0700

tests.title: Every created job has a job_ id of 20 lowercase hex characters, attempts numbered from 1, and millisecond UTC times
given: a jobs store on a temp database
tests.when: for any sequence of created jobs, answers, retries and automatic attempts (seeded generator)
then: every job id matches ^job_[0-9a-f]{20}$ and ids are unique
each job's attempt numbers are 1..k consecutive
every stored and served time matches ^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$
tests.pseudocode: for seq in gen(): run(seq); assert re(id); assert nums == range(1,k+1); assert all(re(t) for t in times)

tests.title: The purge removes expired done, failed and cancelled jobs with their directories and rows, including a job cancelled while queued
given: an injected clock
retain of 1h
done, failed, cancelled-while-queued and cancelled-while-running jobs with finished_at older than retain and attempt directories on disk
tests.when: the clock advances beyond retain and the purge runs, at start and on the hourly tick
then: each expired job's attempts/<job id>/ directory is gone
its rows in af_events, af_attempts and af_jobs are gone
GET /api/v1/jobs/:id answers 404 for each
a job whose finished_at is younger than retain is untouched
tests.pseudocode: clock.Advance(retain+1m); purge(); for j in expired: assert !exists(dir(j)); assert rows(j)==0; assert get(j).status==404

tests.title: The purge keeps blocked jobs, running jobs, in-progress runners and recently cancelled jobs, even when the question is older than retain
given: an injected clock and retain of 1h
a blocked job asked long ago
a job cancelled while blocked whose question is older than retain but whose cancel is recent
a cancelled job whose runner has not returned
a running job
tests.when: the purge runs after the clock passes retain from the question time
then: all four jobs remain readable through GET /api/v1/jobs/:id
their directories and rows remain
after retain passes since the cancel, the cancelled-while-blocked job is purged
tests.pseudocode: purge(); for j in kept: assert get(j).status==200; clock.Advance(retain); purge(); assert get(cancelledWhileBlocked).status==404

tests.title: A purge whose attempts directory cannot be removed keeps the job's rows, logs a WARN naming the job and retries next purge
given: an expired failed job whose attempts directory removal fails (injected remover error)
a captured slog handler
tests.when: the purge runs, then the failure is cleared and the purge runs again
then: after the first purge the job is still readable with status 200 and its rows exist
a WARN record names the job id
after the second purge the directory and rows are gone and GET answers 404
tests.pseudocode: fs.failRemove = true; purge(); assert get(j).status==200; assert warn(j); fs.failRemove=false; purge(); assert get(j).status==404

tests.title: The documentation files name the jobs terms the spec requires
given: the docs directory
tests.when: a docs test reads api.md, configuration.md, model-usage.md, architecture.md and development.md
then: api.md mentions the jobs routes, body limits, SSE, invalid_state, duplicate_job, not_subscribed and token_unreadable
configuration.md mentions [workers] count and [database] retain
model-usage.md mentions automatic attempts, brain, no_result and summed usage
architecture.md mentions the job states, queue key, runner contract, transient retries and event log
development.md mentions the jobs package
tests.pseudocode: for file, terms in required: for t in terms: assert t in read(file)

tests.title: Every single-job response and list entry carries exactly the documented fields, and blocked is an object only while blocked
given: a service with the fake hub and a scripted fake runner
one queued, one blocked (options X, Y, Z), one done job
tests.when: each job is read through GET /jobs/:id and GET /jobs
then: the key set of each document equals the 12 documented plus list fields: id, workspace, kind, input, issue, source, request_label, state, blocked, attempt_count, current_attempt, result, artifacts, side_effects, labels, usage, hub, created_at, started_at, finished_at
input holds no context
request_label is null for API-created jobs
blocked for the blocked job is {reason needs_human, question, options with ids A, B, C, answer_with 'POST /api/v1/jobs/<id>/answer'}
blocked is null in the queued and done jobs
tests.pseudocode: doc = get(id); assert keys(doc)==FIELDS; assert doc.request_label==null; assert blocked.options.ids==['A','B','C']

tests.title: result, artifacts and side_effects come from the latest finished attempt's envelope with exit_code matching the status
given: a job whose attempt 1 ended failed and attempt 2 ended done with two artifacts and one side effect
another job with no finished attempt
tests.when: both jobs are read
then: the first job's result is {status done, exit_code 0, summary, error null} from attempt 2
its artifacts and side_effects are those of attempt 2
the second job has result null and both arrays []
for every finished job result.exit_code equals toolio.ExitCode(result.status)
tests.pseudocode: assert doc.result.exit_code == ExitCode(doc.result.status); assert unfinished.result==null and unfinished.artifacts==[]

tests.title: A job's usage equals the sum of cost, input tokens, output tokens and turns over its finished attempts
given: a jobs store
tests.when: for any job with 1 to 6 finished attempts whose envelopes carry random non-negative usage
then: usage.cost_usd, input_tokens, output_tokens and turns equal the sums over the attempts' usage
an unfinished attempt contributes nothing
tests.pseudocode: for jobs in gen(): assert doc.usage.turns == sum(a.usage.turns for a in finished)

tests.title: started_at is set at first claim and finished_at is set exactly in done, failed and cancelled and cleared when the job queues again
given: a service with a fake runner
jobs driven to done, failed, cancelled-from-queued and cancelled-from-blocked
an injected clock
tests.when: each job is read at every step, then answered, retried and given an automatic attempt
then: started_at is null while queued and set at the first claim, and unchanged by later claims
finished_at is non-null exactly when state is done, failed or cancelled, including cancel from queued or blocked
finished_at of a job cancelled while blocked is the cancel time, not the question time
answer, retry and an automatic attempt clear finished_at to null
tests.pseudocode: assert (doc.finished_at!=null) == (doc.state in {done,failed,cancelled})

tests.title: labels shows set, removed and restore, or null, and hub shows the running attempt's references only while it runs
given: a fake runner that reports hub references (session, run, sandbox) and labels set/removed through the recorder, then blocks
a job with no label activity

after the attempt ends hub is null
labels carries set and removed as last reported with restore null
a job with no label values has labels null
the cancelled job with request label X has labels.restore X
tests.pseudocode: rec.Hub(s,r,b); assert get(id).hub=={s,r,b}; release(); assert get(id).hub==null

tests.title: GET /jobs/:id adds attempts ordered by n with trigger, answer, deliveries, transient failures, outcome fields and times

the list entries carry no attempts field

tests.title: Valid triage (issue, text with title, file) and fix bodies each create a queued job with source api and null request_label
given: the fake hub where the caller sees widgets

source is {kind api, by the hub user id} and request_label is null
kind is triage or fix as routed and issue is 7, null, null and 42

tests.title: Each invalid field is refused with 400 invalid_request naming the field and nothing is stored

tests.when: requests are posted with: empty/whitespace text; invalid UTF-8; NUL byte; text of MaxInputBytes+1; title with a newline; 257-byte title; file.name with / or NUL or empty or 256 bytes; 11 context strings; an empty context string; a 8 KiB+1 string; context totalling over 32 KiB; none or two of issue/text/file; an unknown field

tests.title: An issue value is accepted exactly for a positive integer, an issue URL that is not a pull or merge request, or <path>#<N>
given: the issue parser
tests.when: for any generated issue value: integers (negative, zero, fraction, huge), GitHub and GitLab issue, pull and merge request URLs, other URLs, <path>#<N> strings with 1, 2 or more segments and bad characters, strings over 2048 bytes
then: accepted values yield the issue number from the integer, URL or #N
every other value is refused and the route answers 400 naming issue
tests.pseudocode: for v in gen(): n, ok = ParseIssue(v); assert ok == oracle(v); if ok: assert n == oracleNumber(v)

tests.title: The maximal valid bodies escaped as \u00XX answer 202, and bodies over each route's limit answer 413
given: a subscribed workspace
a triage body of 128 KiB text, 32 KiB context and 256-byte title with every byte \u00XX escaped

an 8 KiB answer escaped byte by byte on the answer route is accepted (not 413)

tests.title: Invisible, unsubscribed, unsubscribing, unreadable-token and duplicate-issue requests are refused with the specified codes

a workspace with an unreadable token
an open fix job for issue 42 on widgets

tests.title: The job row, attempt 1 row and queued job_state event are stored together or not at all, and enqueue happens after the commit

tests.title: The Go entry points create a job with a label source and request label, apply the routes' refusals, and look up the open job
given: a subscribed workspace, an unsubscribed one, and an existing open fix job for issue 42

tests.title: An attempt is one queue item keyed by workspace with nonce <job id>:<n>, and enqueuing it again is a no-op in every item state

a fake runner that blocks

tests.title: No more than [workers].count attempts are ever in the runner at once

tests.title: Jobs on one workspace never overlap and run in enqueue order, while jobs on two workspaces overlap with count 2

tests.title: A transient backoff keeps its workspace's place without a worker slot, and an overrunning runner keeps both place and slot
given: [workers].count = 1
an injected backoff and grace

tests.title: A handover moves attempt and job to running, adds one delivery, emits attempt_start and calls the runner, atomically

tests.title: A claim for a missing job, a job that is not queued or running, or an attempt that is not queued or running acknowledges the item without calling the runner

tests.title: The runner is given the context, ids, handover count, job inputs, context strings, answered questions in order, source, request label and a pre-created absolute attempt directory

tests.title: The exported cancel predicate is true for cancel and unsubscribe causes and false for shutdown

tests.title: Concurrent recorder calls under the race detector produce gap-free seqs, and hub references show in the job during the run

tests.title: A runner result carries envelope, report text, labels set and removed and max attempts, where max 0 means 2

tests.title: The placeholder runner fails every attempt as unsupported, not retryable

result.error.category is unsupported and retryable is false

tests.title: The exported fake runner scripts return, plain error, transient failure, panic and blocking per call and records every call's inputs

tests.title: A finished attempt stores envelope.json and a non-empty report.md with mode 0600, emits attempt_end and updates the job

tests.title: When the job was cancelled meanwhile, the attempt is recorded cancelled, labels follow the runner and restore clears when the runner set the request label

tests.title: done, and unverified with an outcome other than parked, record the attempt and the job done

tests.title: A retryable brain or no_result failure queues an automatic attempt with the same context and answers, bounded by the runner's maximum

a job that has an earlier answer
